levels.name: Bella, 24, Accounting Intern
levels.story: The 8 levels of absurd cleaning procrastination. Level 1. Level one. 140 minutes spent scrubbing my oven while my final exam starts in twenty minutes. I am Bella, a stressed-out blueberry with blue skin, wearing a stained oversized hoodie and holding an old toothbrush. My tiny apartment is drowning in laundry, yet every tile in the bathroom shines like a diamond. How are you polishing grout when your rent is five days overdue? You can scrub all you want, but your bank account is still empty. I clutch the toothbrush tighter, blinking back tears as the glowing digits on my forehead suddenly flicker and drop by twenty minutes. Why did my timer reset right when I needed it most? Suddenly, a loud knock echoes through the hallway, and the door swings open to reveal my landlord inspecting my dust-free walls with utter disdain. He points directly at my unopened textbooks while shaking his head in total disbelief. If I do not pass this exam today, I will literally be homeless by tomorrow morning. My heart races as a sudden chill runs down my spine. You'll see that in Level 2.

levels.name: Sam, 29, Freelance Writer
levels.story: The 8 levels of absurd cleaning procrastination. Level 2. Level two. 450 minutes deep into organizing my sock drawer by fabric density instead of writing my article. I am Sam, a nervous orange-man with bright citrus skin, wearing a neon green apron and holding a label maker. My deadline was two hours ago, but these socks refuse to stay unsorted. Are you seriously color-coding socks when our electricity is about to get cut? Get out of my way before I throw your entire wardrobe into the street. I freeze, my label maker buzzing in my hand as the bright digital number on my forehead flashes and suddenly jumps to zero. Why did the machine wipe my entire cleaning progress instantly? Without any warning, the power grid in the building shuts down completely, plunging my meticulously organized apartment into total darkness. My laptop screen flickers and dies, destroying three hours of unsaved work in a single second. I realize with utter horror that my extreme cleaning obsession has completely sabotaged my livelihood. A sinister shadow appears in the doorway. You'll see that in Level 3.

levels.name: Maya, 32, Graphic Designer
levels.story: The 8 levels of absurd cleaning procrastination. Level 3. Level three. 890 minutes spent waxing the hardwood floors with organic lavender oil instead of sending client revisions. I am Maya, an avocado-woman with soft green skin, wearing rubber cleaning gloves and holding a professional buffer. My client has called twelve times, but the grain of this oak needs absolute perfection. You call this professional work? Your design files are empty, yet your floor is reflecting my face! Give me that back or I'll cancel your contract right now! I gasp, clutching the floor buffer as my forehead display suddenly shifts from 890 to 40 minutes. Why did my timer crash after she touched the sponge? Suddenly, a massive crack echoes beneath my feet as the freshly polished wood begins to splinter apart from the excess moisture. The entire floor caves in slightly, revealing a hidden compartment filled with overdue invoices I had completely forgotten about. My professional reputation vanishes into thin air right before my eyes. I am completely ruined. You'll see that in Level 4.

levels.name: Leo, 26, App Developer
levels.story: The 8 levels of absurd cleaning procrastination. Level 4. Level four. 1,450 minutes spent disinfecting every single key on my mechanical keyboard with isopropyl alcohol instead of launching the app. I am Leo, a yellow lemon-man with a sharp citrus peel, wearing wire-rimmed glasses and holding a cotton swab. The app launch was scheduled for dawn, but the spacebar still has dust particles. Are you really cleaning when our server budget expires in ten minutes? Get out of my chair so I can fix your code! I push my glasses up, glaring at her as my glowing forehead number suddenly drops by half. Why did my hours vanish the second she touched my keyboard? Out of nowhere, the main server terminal emits a piercing alarm as our entire startup platform crashes due to a missed deployment window. All our hard work vanishes from the cloud in a single catastrophic glitch. I stare blankly at the screen as my co-founder walks in with a final termination notice. There is no turning back now. You'll see that in Level 5.

levels.name: Chloe, 28, Podcast Host
levels.story: The 8 levels of absurd cleaning procrastination. Level 5. Level five. 2,300 minutes spent steam-cleaning the wallpaper patterns instead of recording episode fifty. I am Chloe, a fuzzy peach-woman with velvety pink skin, wearing a retro housewife dress and holding a steaming wand. My listeners are waiting, but these floral walls have hidden grease stains. Are you out of your mind? Your sponsors just pulled out because you missed three upload dates! Stop playing domestic goddess and turn on the microphone! I gasp, gripping the steam wand as my glowing forehead number instantly plummets by a thousand. Why did my timer crash right when he insulted my wallpaper? Suddenly, the studio ceiling speaker short-circuits and broadcasts a live feed of my silence to ten thousand angry listeners worldwide. My entire podcast network drops me on the spot, canceling my contract with immediate effect. Panic sets in as I realize my cleaning addiction has cost me everything. I am completely speechless. You'll see that in Level 6.

levels.name: Victor, 41, Luxury Real Estate Broker
levels.story: The 8 levels of absurd cleaning procrastination. Level 6. Level six. 4,100 minutes spent polishing the brass doorknobs in my penthouse instead of closing the multi-million dollar sale. I am Victor, a wealthy lemon-man with polished yellow skin, wearing an Italian pinstripe suit and holding a microfiber cloth. My phone is ringing with buyers, but these hinges have microscopic smudges. You call yourself a top broker while your desk is buried in dust? Clean up this mess before my investors arrive! I stare in sheer disbelief, my gold cloth trembling as my forehead display drops by two thousand minutes. Why did my luxury timer crash so violently? Without warning, the penthouse smart-lock system malfunctions and locks all the exterior doors, trapping my wealthiest investors outside in the hallway. They assume I am incompetent and walk away from the multi-million dollar deal forever. My career as a top broker crumbles into dust in mere seconds. I am utterly ruined. You'll see that in Level 7.

levels.name: Madame Pitaya, 45, Art Collector
levels.story: The 8 levels of absurd cleaning procrastination. Level 7. Level seven. 7,800 minutes spent sanitizing every picture frame in the gallery with organic alcohol instead of opening the exhibition. I am Madame Pitaya, a pink and green dragonfruit-woman with spiky outer leaves, wearing a haute couture gown and holding a velvet feather duster. VIP guests are arriving in minutes, but the gilded frames lack absolute luster. Are you insane? Your entire art collection is locked in storage while collectors wait outside! Open this vault right now or I'm walking away! I freeze, my velvet duster dropping as my forehead display instantly crashes by four thousand minutes. Why did my elite timer collapse right at that second? Suddenly, the gallery fire sprinklers trigger above us, releasing a massive torrent of water that instantly ruins every single priceless painting on display. Millions of dollars in art history dissolve into colorful mush right before our eyes. The ultimate disaster has finally arrived. There is no escape from this. You'll see that in Level 8.
